title: Canonical map from the generation locus of a line module into relative Proj
statement: Let $S,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $f:X\to T$ a morphism over $S$. Let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal A_d$ be a quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal O_T$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra] [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], let $L$ be a line module on $X$, and let $\psi:f^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{d\geq0}L^{\otimes d}$ be a graded algebra homomorphism on the small etale site, with tensor pullback $f^*$ along the induced ringed-topos map. Let $U(\psi)\subseteq X$ be the union over $d\geq1$ of the loci where $\psi_d:f^*\mathcal A_d\to L^{\otimes d}$ is surjective. This is an open subspace, and there is a canonical $T$-morphism $r_{L,\psi}:U(\psi)\to\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$ [def-nagata-relative-proj]. For any commutative diagram of $S$-spaces\n$$\begin{array}{ccc} X' &\xrightarrow{g'}& X\\ f'\downarrow &&\downarrow f\\ T'&\xrightarrow{g}&T,\end{array}$$\nwhere $X'$ and $T'$ are schemes and $g,g'$ are arbitrary morphisms, put $\mathcal A'=g^*\mathcal A$, let $L'=(g')^*L$, and let $\psi'$ be the pulled-back graded homomorphism. Then $U(\psi')=(g')^{-1}(U(\psi))$, and under the canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{Proj}_{T'}(\mathcal A')\simeq T'\times_T\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$ the map $r_{L',\psi'}$ is the base change of $r_{L,\psi}$. On schemes this is the usual canonical morphism obtained from the graded maps into tensor powers of an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], with pullback [def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Tag 0D2Z (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj), opening definition of U(psi) and parts (2),(3), specialized to a scheme base T; Constructions Tag 01O9 (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj).

proof.text: Choose a representable jointly surjective etale scheme cover $V\to X$ from the definition of an algebraic space, then refine $V$ by affine opens over affine opens of $T$ and by etale trivializations of the line module $L$. On a chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}(B)\to X$ over $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, write the trivialized line module as $\mathcal O_W$. For every positive-degree local section $a$ of $f^*\mathcal A_d$, its image $\psi_d(a)$ is a function on $W$, and the locus where $a$ generates the target is the principal open $D(\psi_d(a))$: a map to an invertible module is surjective exactly where one local image is a unit. These principal opens cover the locus where $\psi_d$ is surjective, and their union over $d\geq1$ is therefore open. On $V\times_XV$ the two pullbacks of each such principal open agree, because both are defined by the pullback of the same section and surjectivity of a map of sheaves is local on the etale site. Thus the chartwise opens carry a canonical descent datum; the sheaf definition of the algebraic space gives the descended open subspace $U(\psi)$, and its pullback to every scheme over $X$ is the same union of principal opens. On each such principal open, the affine relative-Proj construction (Constructions, Tag 01O9) gives the canonical morphism to $\operatorname{Proj}(A)$; the affine-chart identifications in [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists] identify these targets with the restriction of $\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Tag 0D2Z, opening construction of U(psi); Constructions Tag 01O9, affine construction and standard opens

proof.text: On a refinement of two affine and trivializing charts, the two local morphisms just constructed have the same homogeneous-fraction formulas on every standard Proj chart. The uniqueness clause in the affine construction therefore identifies them on overlaps, and the same equality holds after pullback to $V\times_XV$. To descend the map, let $W\to U(\psi)$ be any scheme and choose an etale cover $W_i\to W$ factoring through the presentation $V\to X$. The local maps $W_i\to\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$ agree on every $W_i\times_WW_j$ by the overlap equality, so the sheaf condition for the target algebraic space glues them uniquely to a map $W\to\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$. This construction is functorial in $W$, hence defines the unique morphism $r_{L,\psi}$; the structural map to $T$ agrees locally and therefore globally. Pullback to the jointly surjective presentation detects equality, so both the map and its homogeneous-algebra compatibility are unique.

source.place: Tag 0D2Z, construction and uniqueness of r_{L,psi}; Constructions Tag 01O9, parts (1),(2),(3)

proof.text: For an arbitrary commutative square with $X'$ and $T'$ schemes, pullback of the local charts, the graded algebra, the line module, and $\psi$ gives precisely $(\mathcal A',L',\psi')$. Surjectivity of a sheaf map and invertibility of a local generator are preserved and reflected after pullback, so the principal-open description in Step 1 gives $U(\psi')=(g')^{-1}(U(\psi))$. The unrestricted comparison [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] gives the canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{Proj}_{T'}(\mathcal A')\simeq T'\times_T\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$ for this arbitrary $g$, with no flatness assumption. On every pulled-back affine chart, the homogeneous-fraction formula is the pullback of the original formula; by the uniqueness and descent argument of Step 2 these local equalities identify $r_{L',\psi'}$ with the base change of $r_{L,\psi}$.

source.place: Tag 0D2Z, part (3); Constructions Tag 01O9, part (3); relative-Proj base change

proof.text: When $X$ is a scheme, the small-etale line module is the usual invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and the tensor pullback in the statement agrees with the ordinary module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. The preceding affine construction is then exactly the usual canonical morphism obtained from graded maps into tensor powers of an invertible module.
